clue.text: Article on East by leading travel writer

indicators.note: leading puts the travel word at the front of the rest

parts.note: to go is to travel

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper item on the Orient by a top travel journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travel writer' reads as one phrase, but 'writer' alone is the definition; 'leading' puts GO first.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe was the great German poet, novelist and playwright.

clue.text: Method of playing quietly in oriental orchestra

indicators.note: in means the soft letter goes inside the orchestra

parts.note: a gamelan is an Indonesian percussion orchestra
p, piano, is the music term for quietly

explanation.surface: A soft playing style in an Eastern ensemble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Method of playing' suggests music, but it means strategy in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is a plan for how a team will approach a match.

clue.text: General ordered to increase range of shot

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A general orders his gunners to fire further.
explanation.walkthrough: The military picture misleads: the shot is a photograph; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a print bigger expands a photograph's scale.

clue.text: Hasten soundly with stick's heavy blow

indicators.note: soundly signals that the word for hasten is said aloud

parts.note: to hurry is to hasten
a cane is a stick

explanation.surface: Rushing forward to deliver a hefty stroke with a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurricane is a violent storm wind, a gale of the strongest force.

clue.text: Stays to poke fun at painters

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or ridicule them
a painter is a rope that ties a boat to a mooring

explanation.surface: Someone props up artists only to mock them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painters' suggests artists but means boat ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a rope or wire bracing a mast or tent, which is the job of tent guys.

clue.text: Where to name witness not telling the whole story

definitions.meaning: on a document a witness signs below the written account
saying less than the truth, playing something down

explanation.surface: A witness's evidence that leaves part of the story out.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature goes beneath a written declaration, and a description that minimises facts is a deliberate playing-down.

clue.text: Chap often getting out after an over

definitions.text: often getting out after an over
definitions.meaning: in radio talk, a word of acknowledgment often precedes over and out

explanation.surface: A cricketer is regularly dismissed after an over.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture misleads: this is radio procedure, ending 'over and out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger is a man's name and the radio word for message received.

clue.text: Charge added to money for cargo

indicators.note: added to puts the charge word after the money word

parts.note: pay is money earned
a load is a charge, as of a gun

explanation.surface: A fee plus wages for carrying goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A payload is the goods or passengers a vehicle carries.

clue.text: In extreme discomfort, consequently take it easy

parts.note: so means therefore or consequently
to rest is to relax

explanation.surface: Being in great pain, you should therefore relax.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore means painful, and the superlative is the most painful.

clue.text: George I implicated in gun conspiracy?

parts.note: an automatic is a self-loading gun

indicators.note: implicated in means the letter is involved inside the plot word

parts.note: a plot is a conspiracy
taken as written

explanation.surface: King George I accused of a gunpowder plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George I' reads as a king; George is the nickname for an aircraft autopilot.
explanation.definitionFit: George is airmen's slang for the device that flies a plane unaided.

clue.text: Get the most from ball in delivery before receiver is fully alert?

definitions.text: delivery before receiver is fully alert?

parts.note: to milk something is to exploit it to the full
a ball is a bullet, and a round is one shot of ammunition

explanation.surface: Advice to a cricketer on exploiting a ball delivered before the batsman is ready.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture (ball, delivery, receiver) is false: the delivery is of milk to a sleepy householder at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A milkman's early-morning route brings bottles to doorsteps while customers are still half asleep.

clue.text: How one could make a grey composition less grey?

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so these letters are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Asks how a drab grey painting might be brightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' suggests a painting but signals rearranging the letters of A GREY.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey suggests dullness and gloom, so less grey means brighter and more cheerful.

clue.text: Left in charge, one initially provides cover and support

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word one

explanation.surface: Someone left in charge supplies shelter and backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a roofed porch held up by columns, so it both shelters and supports.

clue.text: Umpire's holding jumper gives better protection against the elements

definitions.text: gives better protection against the elements

indicators.note: holding means one word clasps another within it

parts.note: ref is short for referee, an umpire; the 's adds S
a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumping animal

explanation.surface: An umpire wearing a sweater is better shielded from the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a sweater, a British word for a pullover, but it is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a new roof on a building improves its shelter from rain and wind.

clue.text: Brilliant artist's taken back palm

indicators.note: taken back means the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ace means excellent or brilliant
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A brilliant painter's palm has been taken back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken back' turns ACERA round.
explanation.definitionFit: The areca is a tropical palm tree, the source of betel nuts.

clue.text: Return to play part in any response to invaders

indicators.note: in means the reversed piece sits inside the word any

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: Return means the letters for play and part are read backwards

parts.note: to do a part is to play it
a bit is a part or role in a play

explanation.surface: Coming back to perform a role in some reply to attackers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' reverses DOBIT to TIBOD, and 'in' puts that inside ANY; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Antibodies are proteins the immune system makes to fight off invading germs.

clue.text: Boycott brand in Northern city

parts.note: to black goods is to boycott them, in trade-union usage
to brand is to burn a mark into

explanation.surface: Yorkshire cricketer Geoffrey Boycott's brand in a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: Boycott suggests the cricketer; BLACKBURN is a town in Lancashire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackburn is a Lancashire town in the north of England.

clue.text: Short chap, loud one in road displaying rage

indicators.note: in means the chap, loud and one letters sit inside the road

parts.note: Ed is short for Edward
f, forte, is the music term for loud
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A small man shouting in the street, consumed by road rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A flushed face is the outward sign of anger.

clue.text: Man originally leading order

indicators.note: leading puts the name ahead of the next word

parts.note: Ben is a man's name
an edict is an official order

explanation.surface: A man who first headed a religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: St Benedict founded the Benedictine order, so the whole clue also describes him; 'originally' points to that history.
explanation.definitionFit: St Benedict of Nursia founded the Benedictine monks and wrote their Rule.

clue.text: Admission of self-boredom upset retired academics?

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the letters are turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: someone confessing to boring themselves says I tire me

explanation.surface: Retired professors admit to boring themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an emotion but reverses I TIRE ME in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeriti are professors who have retired but keep their honorary title.

clue.text: Correspond with a nameless environmentalist

indicators.note: nameless means the abbreviation for name, the letter N, is dropped

parts.note: a Green is a member of an ecological party

explanation.surface: Writing letters to an anonymous eco-campaigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspond with' suggests letter-writing; N is a standard abbreviation for name.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that correspond match or tally, which is to concur.

clue.text: Pitted valley River Don had formed

indicators.note: formed means the letters are shaped into a new word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A river called the Don carved out a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitted' means full of coal pits: the Rhondda is a Welsh mining valley.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhondda in South Wales was famous for its coal mines.

clue.text: Beloved artist in Modern Times

indicators.note: in means the artist is placed inside the letters for the era

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the modern era
Gustave Doré was a French illustrator

explanation.surface: A much-loved actor in the Chaplin film Modern Times.
explanation.walkthrough: Modern Times is a Chaplin film, but here it is AD, the current era.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beloved is dearly loved, worshipped.

clue.text: Imagine what you might do if sleepwalking

definitions.meaning: to invent or think something up

definitions.text: what you might do if sleepwalking
definitions.meaning: a sleepwalker rises from bed while still dreaming

explanation.surface: Picture what a sleepwalker gets up to.
explanation.definitionFit: To invent a scheme is to conceive it in the mind, and a sleepwalker literally rises while dreaming.

clue.text: Big Ben

parts.note: not the London clock: a ben is a Scottish mountain, and a big one tops 3,000 feet

explanation.walkthrough: Big Ben is the London clock bell; a Munro is a Scottish peak over 3,000 feet, and ben is Scots for mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Scottish peaks above three thousand feet are listed by Sir Hugh's name.

clue.text: Bid without king or queen, and beat it

indicators.note: without means the royal letters are taken away

parts.note: to bid is to make an offer
ER stands for Edwardus Rex or Elizabeth Regina, a king or a queen

explanation.surface: A card player bids with no royal cards and then flees.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge picture misleads: ER are the royal initials on British post boxes and coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for running away hastily.

clue.text: Abdicate, leaving son to rule

indicators.note: leaving means the abbreviation for son departs from the word

parts.note: to abdicate is to resign a throne
S is the genealogy abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A monarch steps down so that their son can be ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's reign is their period of sovereignty.

clue.text: Region organised as one part of deepest Gaul, once

indicators.note: organised means the letters are put into a new order
one part of takes just the opening letter of deepest

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Describes how a region was once administered as part of ancient France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' looks like part of the history but is anagram fodder with GAUL and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Languedoc is a historic region of southern France.

clue.text: Capital radio presenter wants singles at either end of session

parts.note: a DJ, disc jockey, presents on radio

indicators.note: at either end of means a letter is placed at each side of the next word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, so singles gives two of them
a bout is a spell or session

explanation.surface: A Capital Radio DJ wants single records at the start and end of his show.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital Radio is a London station, which hides the definition 'Capital'.
explanation.definitionFit: Djibouti is the capital city of the country of the same name in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Pulled one back towards centre

indicators.note: back means the letters are read from the end to the start

parts.note: drawn means pulled
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone pulled a player back towards the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses DRAWNI.
explanation.definitionFit: Inward means directed to the inside or middle.
